question.text: Regarding the accounting and reporting requirements of social sector organisations (Trusts, Societies, Section 8 Companies), which statements are CORRECT? I. They are all governed under the Companies Act II. They are governed under an Act as per their registration III. They are governed under the SEBI Act IV. There is no single regulatory body for these organisations

explanation.text: The Logic: Statements II and IV are correct per Ch 1.3.1 — each form is governed by its own Act (Trust Act / Societies Act / Companies Act), and there is no single regulatory body. Statement I is wrong (not all under Companies Act). Statement III is wrong (SEBI Act covers SSE-listed entities only, not the constitution of the entity). The Trap: Option A mixes correct (I) with wrong (III). Option C mixes wrong (I) with correct (IV). Option D mixes correct (II) with wrong (III). Only B pairs both correct statements. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to Ch 11 (Key Regulations) and III-A/III-C (Compliance). This is a sample question from the PDF reproduced to test regulatory literacy. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Maintain a 'regulator-matrix' per engagement: columns for (a) constituting Act, (b) tax-exemption regulator, (c) FCRA regulator, (d) SSE regulator, (e) CSR channel. This avoids regulator-confusion findings in peer reviews.
